title: Van Gogh landscape sets $190.4 million artist auction record in Sotheby's sale
summary: In its first appearance at auction, Vincent van Gogh’s Châtaigniers en fleurs sold at Sotheby’s in New York this evening for $190.4 million - a new auction record for the artist and the second highest price for any work of art ever sold at Sotheby's, surpassed only by Gustav Klimt’s Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer, sold here in November 2025 for $236.4 million. Painted in May 1890, just days after Van Gogh’s arrival in Auvers-sur-Oise, Châtaigniers en fleurs dates from the extraordinary period of creative intensity that marked the final two months of the artist’s life, and was among the most important works from this period to have remained in private hands. Offered for sale pursuant to an agreement between the seller and the heirs of the Fischer family, the landmark painting, which had expected to realise in the region of $180 million, formed part of an evening auction dedicated to twelve masterpieces from the legendary Blaquier-Arrieta Collection - a group of Impressionist and Modern

title: Morphy's December 3 Premier Coins & Currency Auction offers 400+ lots
summary: Coin and currency collectors, listen up! Morphy’s will conduct a Premier Coins & Currency Auction on Thursday, December 3rd that deserves your full attention. The catalog features more than 400 lots of rare US and world coins, gold and silver, and collectible currency. Highlights include exceptional Morgan dollars, historic gold coins, early American coinage, and an extraordinary $10,000 Federal Reserve Note. The auction’s expected top lot is the ultra-high-denomination $10,000 Federal Reserve Note (Fr. 2231-B), graded PMG Choice Uncirculated 63. This impressive note comes from the acclaimed Binion’s Casino Horseshoe display in Las Vegas, adding an interesting historical connection to the note’s provenance. It presents beautifully, with generous margins on all four sides, attractive color, and strong overall eye appeal. summary: Roland Auctions NY enjoyed their most-successful auction of the summer and fall seasons on November 14th, through overall sales topping $800,000 hammer, with the exquisite fine jewelry selections, all mainly from a Park Ave. estate collection in Manhattan, generating over $250,000 in their top-sellers alone, featuring jewels by Kwiat, Mario Boschi, Seaman & Schepps, Van Cleef & Arpels, Tiffany, Korloff and others. title: New York's legendary sewer alligator resurfaces in Brooklyn
summary: The alligator is back, and this time, it's here to stay. After making headlines during its 2023 debut in Union Square, NYC Legend, a monumental bronze sculpture by Swedish artist Alexander Klingspor , has found a permanent home on Brooklyn's Gowanus waterfront. The life-size alligator, perched atop a New York City manhole cover, will be celebrated on November 19 as part of the inaugural Gowanus Wharf Block Party at Nevins Landing. For nearly a century, New Yorkers have traded stories of alligators lurking beneath the city's streets. According to the legend, baby alligators brought north from Florida and Louisiana as exotic pets were eventually flushed into the sewers, where they grew into fearsome underground creatures. Whether fact or fiction, the story has proved remarkably difficult to kill. Klingspor was drawn to the staying power of the myth and the creature at its center. title: MoMA announces a major retrospective of Ana Mendieta
summary: The Museum of Modern Art announces Ana Mendieta: A Retrospective, a major exhibition of the interdisciplinary practice of Ana Mendieta (American, b. Cuba, 1948–1985), one of the most consequential artists of her generation. On view at MoMA from December 12, 2027, through April 15, 2028, the exhibition will include approximately 200 artworks and selections of archival material, with key loans from the Estate of Ana Mendieta. The first US retrospective to offer a comprehensive examination of Mendieta's oeuvre in more than 20 years, the MoMA presentation will include rarely exhibited works, from revelatory early paintings to newly remastered films and an in-depth representation of her drawings and sculptures. The exhibition will feature a number of works from MoMA's collection, one of the most distinguished holdings of Mendieta's work

title: Adrián Villar Rojas' monumental sculptures lands in the National Museum of Norway's light hall
summary: Adrián Villar Rojas conceives ambitious, long-term projects that often take the form of large-scale, site-specific environments. Created through extensive collaborations and moving between sculpture, drawing, film, technology, architecture and literature, his projects explore the fate of humanity on the brink of extinction. His installations have transformed museums and landscapes around the world, confronting audiences with a radical question: What will remain of humanity when we are gone? ‘Adrián Villar Rojas. The End of Imagination’ is the Argentine-Peruvian artist’s first exhibition in Norway and the first major presentation of these works in Europe. With this exhibition, the National Museum introduces one of the most ambitious artistic practices on the international contemporary art scene to the Norwegian audience. The exhibition is centred around three monumental sculptures from Villar Rojas’s series The End of Imagination. Suspended between enormous light bo

title: Joan B. Mirviss LTD and Asia Week New York Zoom into the World of Contemporary Japanese Women Ceramic Artists
summary: Joan B. Mirviss LTD and Asia Week New York will co-host a special Zoom webinar on Wednesday, December 2, at 5:00 p.m. (EST), exploring the creation and impact of Radical Clay: Contemporary Women Artists from Japan, the groundbreaking traveling exhibition celebrating Japanese women ceramic artists who have challenged tradition and transformed the possibilities of sculptural expression. Featuring 40 works by 36 artists, Radical Clay brings long-overdue recognition to women whose innovative approaches to form, scale, color, and texture have expanded the boundaries of contemporary Japanese ceramics. title: Sotheby's sales of contemporary art realize $378.7M in one evening
summary: Sotheby’s achieved $378.7 million across its evening of Contemporary sales in New York, marking the auction house’s second-highest total for a contemporary evening series since November 2021 and more than doubling its November 2025 total. Strong international competition pushed more than 60 percent of the offered lots past their high estimates, anchored by a series of new auction records for artists including Yayoi Kusama, Sam Francis, and Jonas Wood. Single-owner collections proved to be the primary engine of the night, generating $239 million—or 60 percent of the evening's overall value. title: Lesley Vance unveils new oil paintings and two-color watercolors at Xavier Hufkens
summary: Xavier Hufkens presents a major solo exhibition by American artist Lesley Vance (b. 1977, Milwaukee, WI), marking her largest exhibition in Europe to date. Spanning the gallery's St-Georges space, the exhibition brings together a substantial body of new oil paintings and watercolours. Her sixth exhibition with the gallery offers an expansive view of Vance's evolving exploration of colour, form and the possibilities of abstraction. There is something strangely familiar about Lesley Vance’s paintings, even when nothing in them can be named. Their sinuous, interlocking forms suggest petals, folds of fabric, fragments of bodies or objects glimpsed at close range, yet none of these associations quite holds. At the heart of Vance’s practice is a sustained questioning of the boundaries between abstraction and representation; she has described her work as “representational painting of something abstract”. title: World records for Max Oppenheimer and Alfons Walde propel Dorotheum's best-ever modern art auction
summary: A spectacular kick-off of the Contemporary Week on 17 November 2026, at the Palais Dorotheum: World records for Max Oppenheimer and Alfons Walde, along with intense international bidding battles, created a highly energized atmosphere in the packed auction hall. With total sales exceeding 10.5 million euros, Dorotheum achieved the best result for a modern art auction in its history. After more than nine decades in private hands, the very first “Musician portrait” of Max Oppenheimer was offered for auction for the first time and sold for a world-record price.* More than ten bidders in the auction room, on the phones, and online vied for the Cubist/Futurist oil painting “The Hess Quartet. title: Christie's New York 20th Century Evening Sale achieves $627 million
summary: Christie's highly-anticipated 20/21 Fall Marquee Week sales began Tuesday, November 17 at Rockefeller Center with the premier auction of the season, the 20th Century Evening Sale. With more than 70 lots spanning 500 years of art history, the sale was energetic and strong, marked by passionate bidding on the phone and online, global bidding including strong bidding from Asia, and record-breaking sales across various categories. The sale totaled $626,621,400, selling 92% by lot and 95% by value. With tonight's sale, Christie's year-to-date 20th and 21st Century Art category in the Americas has already surpassed the category's full-year 2025 total, after just the first night of Marquee Week. title: Hundreds of unseen studio drawings feature in Franz Erhard Walther solo show
summary: There has not been a solo exhibition of Franz Erhard Walther’s drawings in the German speaking area since 1999. Based on the unique collection of the Franz Erhard Walther Foundation, the VILLA will present this complex ensemble from September 27, 2026 until May 9, 2027 in the exhibition DEDICATED TO THE MOON. With hundreds of drawings, including works from the studio that have never before been exhibited, visitors will have the opportunity to discover this extraordinary body of work. For seventy years, drawing has been both the starting point and the place where Franz Erhard Walther realises and develops his radical artistic vision. This multi-layered world of drawing is not merely a companion to the evolution of his work, but stands at its very centre. title: MASI Lugano exhibition program: Cindy Sherman, Franco Vaccari and a new path
summary: The museum as a dynamic organism, called to continually re-imagine its role, its collection, and its spaces: this is the vision that informs MASI's programme for 2027 under the direction of Letizia Ragaglia. The season opens with "Re-imaginings: Mai-Thu Perret and Una Szeemann", which will be followed by a series of exhibitions conceived to combine global and local, inviting contemporary artists to take a fresh, sometimes radical look at the collection. In line with this new vision, the museum's venues are also being redefined: from 2027, the historical Palazzo Reali building will play a complementary role to that of the LAC as a permanent mediation platform, open to the city and welcoming independent organisations working in the visual arts in Ticino. title: Nearly 130 Nuremberg Trial lots, including Documents signed by Göring, Hess and Speer, headline auction
summary: Eighty years after the conclusion of the main Nuremberg trial, nearly 130 lots of original trial papers, including documents signed by Hermann Göring, Rudolf Hess and Albert Speer, headline RR Auction's World War II sale, which closes Nov. 19. Nearly 130 lots of Nuremberg trial papers form the centerpiece of the auction, including witness applications, interrogation transcripts, handwritten letters and signed statements by defendants who faced prosecution for war crimes and crimes against humanity. The documents record their attempts to challenge accusations, distance themselves from responsibility and prepare their defenses before the International Military Tribunal. Among the highlights is a document signed by Hermann Göring on Jan. 15, 1946, requesting testimony intended to establish that he had no knowledge of medical experiments

title: Portland Art Museum marks transformative first year post-expansion with nearly 500,000 visits
summary: One year after opening its $116 million expansion and renovation, the Portland Art Museum has welcomed nearly half a million people, delivering on the promise of contributing to the revitalization of downtown Portland. Following the grand opening of PAM’s transformed campus on November 20, 2025, the opening month alone drew 37,500 visitors as Portlanders took part in grand opening free days and festivities. This week, the Portland Art Museum is celebrating the first year of its expanded campus by offering the community a buy-one-get-one-free ticket promotion from November 17–22. Visitors can also enjoy free events at PAM CUT’s PLUS PLUS Festival. title: Elisa Sighicelli explores the myth of the Amazons in second solo show at Galeria Leme
summary: Galeria Leme presents “Le Amazzoni,” Italian artist Elisa Sighicelli’s second solo exhibition at the gallery. The show brings together 12 previously unseen photographs, printed directly on travertine, depicting fragments of Greco-Roman statues of Amazons and of reliefs featuring Amazonomachies—their battles against the ancient Greeks. On stone, the reproduction of the statues takes on the weight, texture, and volume of a sculptural object: the image, once a record, becomes stone again. “Through photography, matter, and the persistence of a myth, the exhibition questions the way images construct memory, define otherness, and continue to shape how we look at the present,” says the artist. title: Legendary Silver Dollar, a secret mint rarity, sells for $1.952 million
summary: Stack’s Bowers Galleries, America’s oldest rare coin auctioneer and dealer, just sold an 1885 Trade Dollar that shouldn’t exist for $1.952 million. In 1885, a powerful political appointee named A. Loudon Snowden retired, ending a decades-long career at the United States Mint in Philadelphia that saw him relentlessly use his position for personal gain. His career began when his uncle — the former speaker of the Pennsylvania State House and Treasurer of Pennsylvania — gave him a job at age 22, fresh out of college. Over the decades that followed, Snowden oversaw the off-the-books production of thousands of delicacies for coin collectors, enriching himself and others in the process. title: Nara Roesler announces the representation of Maria Dávila and Eduardo Portillo
summary: Nara Roesler and Andrew Kreps Gallery are pleased to announce the co-representation of María Dávila (b. 1966, Mérida, Venezuela) and Eduardo Portillo (b. 1966, Jajó, Venezuela), Venezuelan artists whose collaborative work investigates the intersections of landscape, memory, materiality, and the transmission of cultural knowledge through textile and sculpture. Based in Mérida, in the Venezuelan Andes, the artists have been working together since 1983, developing a distinctive approach to weaving that brings ancestral techniques and artisanal traditions into dialogue with contemporary artistic expression. Rooted in the geography and biodiversity of the Andean region, their work draws on the cultural histories, ecological systems, and forms of knowledge embedded in the territories they inhabit. title: Christie's realizes €4.8 million for Roger Therond photography collection with eleven world records
summary: As the world celebrates the bicentenary of photography, Christie's was honoured to present the legendary collection of Roger Therond, which realised €4,804,480. A highly anticipated event, this tribute sale to “his unique eye and his contribution to the history of photography” was enthusiastically received by the public, attracting more than 3,000 visitors to the exhibition over six days. The four pre-emption acquisitions made by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the Musée d'Orsay and the Musée des Beaux-Arts et d'Archéologie de Besançon underscore the collection's historical and cultural significance. The interest shown by these major institutions, alongside more than twenty acquisitions by international museums, highlights both the exceptional quality of the works offered and their importance in enriching public collections. title: Koller December auctions feature works by Claude Monet, Paul Delvaux, and Albert Anker
summary: Koller’s December auctions bring together a highly attractive selection of Modern, Contemporary and Swiss Art, alongside rare jewellery, collectors’ watches and Asian works of art. Highlights range from a luminous London pastel by Claude Monet and a major Surrealist painting by Paul Delvaux to important works by Augusto Giacometti and Albert Anker, two diamonds of more than 12 carats and a rare Cartier Crash wristwatch. The Impressionist & Modern Art auction on 4 December features a remarkable pastel by Claude Monet, ‘Bateaux sur la Tamise’, created during his visits to London in 1900/01. Fascinated by the city’s ever-changing light and atmosphere, Monet worked tirelessly to capture the fleeting effects of sunlight and fog over the Thames. In this intimate composition, boats emerge from the blue of the river and the surrounding

title: Exhibition at Galeria Jaqueline Martins brings together ten intergenerational artists
summary: Certain times seem nervous. What we call experience is what bodies retain from an effort: the flash of a nerve contracting or relaxing. Time Is an Emotional Muscle begins with this suspicion: time is a form of the body’s excitation; its spirit, its zeitgeist, the rhythms of history understood as a tense nervous system. The exhibition brings together artists of different generations and approaches who share less a common theme than a particular insistence: to sustain the tension within the space that separates abstraction from reality, concept from action, and form from the desires we cast as shadows upon the world. Each artist, in their own way, seeks to s t r e t c h the possibilities of a specific moment, a particular state of affairs. The verb also becomes a method: to stretch, to fold, to expand, and to recalibrate the moments of perception through which

title: Beat Wismer curates major Martin Disler retrospective across Galerie Urs Meile's Zurich spaces
summary: Galerie Urs Meile is presenting Under the Volcano, a solo exhibition by Swiss artist Martin Disler (1949–1996), curated by Beat Wismer. Thirty years after his passing, the exhibition celebrates Disler’s artistic legacy across both of the gallery’s Zurich locations. On view from November 19, 2026, to January 9, 2027, the presentation at Rämistrasse will focus on works on paper from 1981 to 1983, while paintings, sculptures and monotypes from 1983 to 1995 will be presented at Ankerstrasse. In its directness, the radical art of the Swiss artist Martin Disler (1949–1996) never tolerated any compromises. With his feverish energy, he pushed himself to the brink of self-destruction throughout his short artistic life. During his relatively brief 25-year career as a visual artist, his uncompromising stance also posed an unrelenting challenge to the art scene of the time.

title: From lab-grown textiles to compost-powered computers - A Matter of Land opens at the Design Museum
summary: The Design Museum is spotlighting seven design research projects that present ecological and regenerative design practices in the new display, A Matter of Land, opening on 19 November 2026. Curated by its national research programme for the green transition, Future Observatory, the display brings together stories of care, restoration and material innovation, organised across three sections: Field, Forest and Earth. Nearly half of all raw materials extracted from the land each year go into making our buildings, clothes and infrastructure. As natural resources come under growing strain, how we design with the land – from soil to the species it supports – has never mattered more. Researchers, designers, scientists, geologists and local communities are developing lasting ways to protect our natural landscapes while continuing to gather essential resources

title: Theaster Gates reconfigures signature materials in new Hong Kong exhibition at Gagosian
summary: Gagosian is presenting Surrogate, an exhibition of new works by Theaster Gates opening at the gallery in Hong Kong on November 19. The surrogate has been ever present in Gates’s practice. Using the bones of an abandoned Chicago building to restore the functions of Huguenot House in Kassel, Germany, for Documenta 13, presenting fire hoses as a proxy for a conversation on civil rights, deploying the charged medium of tar to stand in for the complex relationship between father and son, or repurposing historic archives as a way of countering the invisibility of Black people, art as surrogate makes rich the abundance of meaning available through the materials and processes of his studio.
